label: first copy step echoing an initial a (also p/k)
explanation: Sparse copy-phase feature (99.6% of mass in the copy phase, none at the delimiter, almost none in the original phase). 86% of mass is at recall_idx 1, the first copy step, where the input is the fed-back first original token. Input a carries 67% of mass, p 15%, k 9%. Fires mostly on short sequences (L=3-4 has 11.6x and 3.5x lift). The strongest activations are sequences beginning a p ... or a i l ..., i.e. when the token being output is i or p, and q or l show up later in the sequence. However the feature only fires on a small and hard-to-predict subset of these contexts: recall_idx==1 & in_tok==a has precision 0.06 and mass recall 0.57. Adding p/k raises mass recall to 0.78 but precision drops to 0.03. Restricting out_tok to i/p raises precision to 0.29 but recall falls to 0.19. Later copy steps with input a account for some of the remaining mass. It does not fire in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on first occurrences of tokens. The extra conditioning that decides firing is not captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=p (+4.88), in_tok=k (+4.65), phase=2 & in_tok=a (+3.96), prev_tok=z (+3.95), phase=2 & out_tok=p (+3.31), in_tok=a (+3.18). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.96), orig5=h (-2.29), orig3=h (-1.96), in_first=1 (-1.87).
